mainTopic: What ״כן יעשה״ and ״לפר״ teach about the inner חטאות and the פר יום הכפורים
overview: The גמרא goes through a ברייתא about the blood of the inner חטאות. It first explains that seven sprinklings are indispensable in other places too: the פרה אדומה and the מצורע. It then asks why the four placements on the inner מזבח need their own source, ״כן יעשה״. רבי ירמיה says the source is needed only for רבי שמעון, who counts the four corners as two plus two. רבי יהודה learns all four corners from ״באהל מועד״ and uses ״כן יעשה״ for סמיכה and שירי הדם of the פר יום הכפורים. אביי disagrees and says even רבי יהודה needs ״כן יעשה״ for the four placements. Next the גמרא asks what ״לפר״ teaches about the פר יום הכפורים. רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer is knocked down by a ברייתא, and רב פפא says ״לפר״ carries over three laws: ״את״, ״בדם״, and ״בטבילה״. The explanation of ״את״ begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: seven sprinklings are indispensable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא: we know the seven sprinklings are indispensable, because seven sprinklings are indispensable everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I only know that the seven sprinklings are indispensable, since seven sprinklings are indispensable in every place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא so it can look at it closely. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the seven sprinklings toward the פרוכת cannot be skipped. Its reason is that seven sprinklings are indispensable wherever the תורה requires them. Steps 2-3 explain this reason, and step 4 turns to the four placements.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven sprinklings of blood
Indispensable: if they are missing, the service does not count

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מַתַּן שֶׁבַע
phrases.english: The Master said: I have only the seven placements
phrases.notes: These are the seven sprinklings of blood toward the פרוכת, the curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: which are indispensable in every place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens close study of the ברייתא quoted just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seven sprinklings are indispensable, because seven sprinklings are indispensable everywhere.

steps.title: Where are seven sprinklings indispensable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which cases the ברייתא means when it says seven are indispensable "everywhere."
steps.simpleTranslation: Where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: which cases does "everywhere" mean? This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's reason only works if there are other known cases where seven sprinklings cannot be skipped. The גמרא wants those cases named.

keyTerms.meaning: Where? In which case?

phrases.english: Where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what "everywhere" in step 1 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which other cases have seven sprinklings that cannot be skipped.

steps.title: רב פפא: the red heifer and leprous marks
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that seven sprinklings are indispensable in the פרה אדומה and in the purification of a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: in the red heifer and in leprous marks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא names the two cases where seven sprinklings cannot be skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the פרה אדומה and the טהרה of a מצורע, the תורה requires seven sprinklings and missing any one of them ruins the process. That is the background for the ברייתא's claim that "seven" is indispensable everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: The פרה אדומה, the red heifer
Leprous marks: the purification of a מצורע

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In the red heifer and in leprous marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פרה אדומה and the purification of a מצורע.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: a source for the four placements
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the four placements on the inner מזבח are also indispensable, and answers from ״כן יעשה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the four placements? The פסוק says: "So shall he do."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא. The ברייתא gives a separate source showing the four placements on the inner מזבח cannot be skipped either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "seven is indispensable everywhere" reason only covers the seven sprinklings. So the ברייתא brings the extra words ״כן יעשה״ to teach the same rule for the four placements on the corners of the inner מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The four placements of blood on the corners of the inner מזבח
From where do we know?
"The פסוק teaches": introduces the source

phrases.english: From where do we know the four placements?
The verse states: "So shall he do."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא after the side question about "everywhere."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four placements on the inner מזבח are indispensable, learned from ״כן יעשה״.

steps.title: Why do the four placements need a special source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the four placements are written and repeated just like the seven, so why do they need ״כן יעשה״?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the seven placements? That they are written and repeated? The four placements are also written and repeated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If the seven placements count as indispensable because they are written twice, the four placements are written twice too, so no special source should be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something the תורה writes and then repeats is treated as indispensable. Both the seven sprinklings and the four placements show up in two passages: the bull of the anointed כהן and the bull of the community. So the four should be indispensable for the same reason, and ״כן יעשה״ looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Written and repeated: the תורה says it in two places
Also

phrases.english: What is different about the seven placements?
That they are written and repeated?
phrases.notes: They're written for the anointed כהן's bull, and then written again for the community's bull.

phrases.english: The four placements as well
are written and repeated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's need for a separate source in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of ״כן יעשה״ for the four placements.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being written and repeated already makes something indispensable, and the four placements are written and repeated just like the seven, so the extra source is not needed.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: needed only according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the source for the four placements is needed only according to רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is needed only according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge. The ברייתא's source is needed only for one תנא's view, רבי שמעון's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed all four placements are fully written in each passage. רבי שמעון does not read the פסוקים that way, as the next step shows. So by his view the four are not "written and repeated," and ״כן יעשה״ is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for...

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is needed only according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to one תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed everyone agrees that all four placements are written in both passages.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, the four are not written twice, so the ברייתא needs ״כן יעשה״ to make them indispensable.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's reading: two corners plus two corners
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון learns two corners from each of two passages, adding up to four.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: above it says "corners" instead of "corner", meaning two. Below it again says "corners" instead of "corner", making four. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for רבי ירמיה's answer. It shows how רבי שמעון reads the פסוקים about the corners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural word "קרנות" teaches at least two corners. רבי שמעון takes two from the first passage and two more from the second, so four. Since no single passage teaches all four, the four are never "written and repeated," and that is why ״כן יעשה״ is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Corner / corners of the מזבח
Above / below: the earlier and the later passage

phrases.english: As it is taught: above it says:
phrases.notes: "Above" is the anointed כהן's bull (ויקרא 4:7), and "below" is the community's bull (ויקרא 4:18).

phrases.english: "corner" as "corners": two;
below it says:
"corner" as "corners": four.
These are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי ירמיה's answer by showing רבי שמעון's view.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי שמעון the four placements are not written in full twice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון builds four corners from two plural words in two passages.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: all four corners from ״באהל מועד״
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה says there is no need to add two and two, because ״באהל מועד״ includes every corner of the inner מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It is not necessary. It says "in the אהל מועד", meaning all the corners stated about the אהל מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יהודה, who disagrees with רבי שמעון's method. He learns all four corners from a single phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, ״באהל מועד״ means every corner of the מזבח in the אהל מועד, which is all four. So each passage on its own teaches all four corners. That raises the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary
The Tent of Meeting, where the inner מזבח stood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It is not necessary;
for it says: "in the Tent of Meeting"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:18

phrases.english: on all that is stated about the Tent of Meeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other תנא's view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four corners are learned from ״באהל מועד״, with no need to combine two passages.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with ״כן יעשה״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה learns from ״כן יעשה״, since he does not need it for the four placements.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה, what does he do with "so shall he do"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the extra words ״כן יעשה״ teach according to רבי יהודה. This sets up an answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the four placements are already written in both passages, so they are indispensable without ״כן יעשה״. Every word of a פסוק must teach something, so the גמרא wants to know what this phrase teaches according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה rejects the rule that the four placements are indispensable. He agrees with the rule but gets it a different way, so the question is only about what the words ״כן יעשה״ are for.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda, "so shall he do"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, ״כֵּן יֵעָשֶׂה״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבי יהודה's view in step 8, which leaves ״כן יעשה״ without a job.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה learns from the phrase ״כן יעשה״.

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses the phrase for the פר יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses ״כן יעשה״ to teach that סמיכה and pouring the leftover blood apply to the פר יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches: we did not learn that the פר יום הכפורים needs סמיכה, or what to do with its leftover blood. Where do we learn it from? The פסוק says ״כן יעשה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. רבי יהודה uses ״כן יעשה״ for a different lesson: the פר יום הכפורים also needs סמיכה and pouring out of the leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already learns all four corners from ״באהל מועד״, so ״כן יעשה״ is free for another teaching. A ברייתא uses it to bring two extra steps to the פר יום הכפורים: סמיכה and שירי הדם.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered
The blood left over after the sprinklings, which is poured on the base of the מזבח
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
"So shall he do", the phrase being discussed

phrases.english: He needs it for that which is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא לָמַדְנוּ לְפַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
phrases.english: Since we did not learn regarding the bull of Yom Kippur
that it needs leaning of hands,
and the leftover blood, from where do we know it?
The verse says: "So shall he do."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה learns from ״כן יעשה״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: That the פר יום הכפורים needs סמיכה and pouring out of the leftover blood

steps.title: Didn't we already learn about the פר יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the ברייתא itself already learned the פר יום הכפורים from ״לפר״, so why is ״כן יעשה״ needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And did we not learn about the פר יום הכפורים? But you said earlier: ״לפר״ refers to the פר יום הכפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 10. The same ברייתא already said that the word ״לפר״ brings in the פר יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״לפר״ already compares the פר יום הכפורים to the bull for a communal mistake, then all its steps should already apply. So ״כן יעשה״ seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: "To the bull", a word in the verse used to include the פר יום הכפורים
But you said, which points back to an earlier statement

phrases.english: And regarding the bull of Yom Kippur, did we not learn it?
But you said:
"To the bull": this is the bull of Yom Kippur!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:20

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְפַר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים לֹא לָמַדְנוּ? הָא אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for ״כן יעשה״ to teach about the פר יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״לפר״ already includes the פר יום הכפורים, so a second source would be extra

steps.title: The extra source covers steps that do not hold back atonement
steps.stepSummary: Without ״כן יעשה״ we might think ״לפר״ only covers steps that are needed for atonement, and not סמיכה or שירי הדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: that comparison applies only to a service that holds back atonement. But a service that does not hold back atonement, say it does not apply. So the verse teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. ״לפר״ alone might only cover the essential steps, so ״כן יעשה״ is needed for the extra ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some steps, like sprinkling the blood, are required for the atonement to work. Others, like סמיכה and pouring the leftover blood, are not. ״לפר״ could be read as covering only the first kind, so ״כן יעשה״ adds the second kind.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
It could enter your mind to say, which introduces a mistaken first thought
A service without which there is no atonement
It teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: ״לפר״ brings the essential steps to the פר יום הכפורים, and ״כן יעשה״ adds the non-essential ones: סמיכה and שירי הדם.

phrases.english: It was needed;
it could enter your mind to say:
these words apply only to a service that holds back atonement,
phrases.notes: If this step is skipped, the atonement doesn't work.

phrases.english: but a service that does not hold back atonement,
say it does not apply;
so the verse teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the first source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לפר״ covers only the steps that hold back atonement
steps.terutzMaskana: ״כן יעשה״ adds even the steps that do not hold back atonement

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון learn from "in the Tent of Meeting"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון does with ״באהל מועד״, since he does not use it for the four corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון, what does he do with this phrase "in the Tent of Meeting"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. רבי יהודה used ״באהל מועד״ for all four corners, so what does רבי שמעון learn from those words?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learns the four corners as two plus two from two passages. So ״באהל מועד״ seems to have no job for him, and the גמרא asks what it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: "In the Tent of Meeting"
What does he do with it? This asks what a תנא learns from a phrase

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון,
this phrase "in the Tent of Meeting", what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, הַאי ״בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 9, now asking about רבי שמעון
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי שמעון learns from ״באהל מועד״

steps.title: No sprinkling if the היכל roof has a hole
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from ״באהל מועד״ that if the roof of the היכל is broken open, the כהן does not sprinkle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs "in the Tent of Meeting" to teach that if the roof of the היכל was breached, he would not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון uses ״באהל מועד״ for a different law. The sprinkling may only be done while the היכל is whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sprinkling must be done "in the Tent of Meeting". If the roof has a hole, the place no longer counts as a proper אהל מועד, so the sprinkling cannot be done.

keyTerms.meaning: Was broken open or breached
Roof or ceiling
The Sanctuary building where the inner מזבח stands
Sprinkles the blood

phrases.english: He needs "in the Tent of Meeting" to teach
that if the roof of the היכל was breached,
he would not sprinkle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״באהל מועד״ teaches that no sprinkling is done if the roof of the היכל has a hole

steps.title: Where רבי יהודה learns the roof rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the roof rule from the extra word ״אשר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי יהודה? He learns it from "which is".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers in a few words. רבי יהודה used ״באהל מועד״ for the four corners, so he learns the roof rule from the word ״אשר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says "the מזבח which is in the Tent of Meeting". רבי יהודה treats the word "which" as extra, so it can teach a law of its own, the roof rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, which asks about the other תנא's view
"Which" or "that is", a small word in the verse

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה: where does he learn the roof rule?

phrases.english: He learns it from "which is".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where רבי יהודה finds the law of Step 14, and answers right away
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns the roof rule from the word ״אשר״

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not learn from the word "which"
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not learn laws from the word ״אשר״, so he needs ״באהל מועד״ for the roof rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי שמעון? He does not expound "which is".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי שמעון cannot learn the roof rule from ״אשר״ the way רבי יהודה does. He simply does not learn laws from that word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two תנאים argue about whether ״אשר״ is extra enough to teach a law. רבי יהודה says yes, so ״באהל מועד״ is free for the four corners. רבי שמעון says no, so ״באהל מועד״ must teach the roof rule, and he learns the corners as two plus two.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not expound, meaning he does not learn a law from this word

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns the four corners from ״באהל מועד״ and the roof rule from ״אשר״. רבי שמעון does not learn from ״אשר״, so he learns the roof rule from ״באהל מועד״ and the four corners as two plus two.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now it's רבי שמעון: why doesn't he learn it from ״אשר״ too?

phrases.english: He does not expound "which is".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי שמעון does not use the source from Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון does not learn laws from ״אשר״, so ״באהל מועד״ is needed for the roof rule

steps.title: אביי: Even for רבי יהודה the phrase is needed
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even according to רבי יהודה, ״כן יעשה״ is needed. Otherwise we might think the four placements are like סמיכה and שירי הדם, which are not indispensable even though the תורה writes and repeats them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even according to רבי יהודה it was needed. You might have thought: just like leaning hands on the animal and the leftover blood are not indispensable, even though the תורה writes them and repeats them, so too the four placements of blood would not be indispensable. So the פסוק teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי goes back to the challenge of step 5 and answers it differently from רבי ירמיה. He says that even רבי יהודה needs ״כן יעשה״, to show that the four placements of blood are indispensable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating something in the תורה does not by itself make it indispensable, as we see from סמיכה and שירי הדם. So we might have grouped מתן ארבע with them. ״כן יעשה״ breaks that comparison and teaches that the four placements are required.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed
Leaning one's hands on the animal before it is slaughtered
The leftover blood, poured out at the base of the מזבח after the sprinklings
They are repeated (written twice)
The four placements of blood
Does not hold things back; not indispensable

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that anything the תורה repeats is automatically indispensable. אביי's whole point is that סמיכה and שירי הדם are repeated and still are not.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
According to Rabbi Yehuda too, it was needed;
phrases.notes: "It" means the words ״כן יעשה״, which teach that the four placements are required.

phrases.english: it might have entered your mind to say:
just as it is with leaning hands and the leftover blood,
that even though they are written and repeated,
they are not indispensable,
so too the four placements should not be indispensable;
so it teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נָמֵי אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the קשיא of step 5 and offers an alternative to רבי ירמיה's answer in step 6. ״כן יעשה״ is needed for the four placements even according to רבי יהודה, not only according to רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the phrase is needed to block a mistaken comparison (מידי דהוה) to סמיכה and שירי הדם.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being written and repeated does not prove the four placements are indispensable, since סמיכה and שירי הדם are written and repeated yet not indispensable. So one might think the four placements are not indispensable either.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״כן יעשה״ teaches that the four placements are indispensable.

steps.title: What does ״לפר״ teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that ״לפר״ refers to the bull of יום הכפורים and asks which law this teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״To the bull״: this is the bull of יום הכפורים. For what law is this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the ברייתא and asks what practical law it teaches. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares the פר העלם דבר to the bull of יום הכפורים. The גמרא wants to know exactly what this comparison adds.

keyTerms.meaning: "To the bull" (from the פסוק)
The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום הכפורים
For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: "To the bull": this is the bull of Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:20. The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא again.

phrases.english: For what law is this needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ״כן יעשה״ to the next phrase in the ברייתא, ״לפר״.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law the ברייתא learns by connecting ״לפר״ to the bull of יום הכפורים.

steps.title: If it teaches that things are required, that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If ״לפר״ teaches that the details are indispensable, the line seems unnecessary, because the bull of יום הכפורים already has the word ״חקה״, which makes its details indispensable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is meant to teach that the details are indispensable, that's obvious, because ״חקה״ is written about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא guesses one possible purpose and immediately challenges it. The word ״חקה״ already makes the יום הכפורים service indispensable, so what does ״לפר״ add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that wherever the תורה says ״חקה״, the details must be done exactly. Since the יום הכפורים service is called ״חקת עולם״, it already has that status, so ״לפר״ seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: To make it indispensable
It's obvious
A statute; a word that makes the details indispensable

phrases.english: If it is meant to teach that it is indispensable, that is obvious,
since "statute" is written about it!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries out one answer to the question in step 18 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement ״לפר — זה פר יום הכפורים״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bull of יום הכפורים already has ״חקה״, so its details are already indispensable. The derivation from ״לפר״ is unnecessary.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: Needed for רבי יהודה, who limits ״חקה״
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that ״לפר״ is needed according to רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה holds that ״חקה״ applies only to the services done in white garments inside the קודש הקדשים: if those are done out of order, nothing was accomplished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is needed only according to רבי יהודה. He says that ״חקה״ is written only about the things done in white garments inside. If the כהן גדול did one of those before another, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins his answer. He explains that according to רבי יהודה, the word ״חקה״ covers only the inside services of יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that ״חקה״ covers everything in the יום הכפורים service. רבי יהודה limits it to the inside services, and for those even the order is indispensable. This leaves the outside services without ״חקה״, which sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for...
The white linen garments the כהן גדול wears for the special יום הכפורים services
Inside, in the קודש הקדשים
He has done nothing at all

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is needed only according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: when "statute" is written,
it is about the things done in white garments inside,
phrases.notes: "Inside" means in the קודש הקדשים, where the incense is burned and the blood sprinkled.

phrases.english: so that if he did one action before another,
he has done nothing at all;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by narrowing what ״חקה״ covers according to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the source (״חקה״) according to one תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״חקה״ covers the entire יום הכפורים service, so ״לפר״ is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, ״חקה″ covers only the inside services, so another source is needed for the rest.

steps.title: Outside services: order does not matter, so ״לפר″ is needed for the sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: For the services done in white garments outside, doing them out of order still counts. So we might have thought the sprinklings themselves are not indispensable either, and ״לפר״ teaches that they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the things done in white garments outside, if he did one action before another, what he did counts. So you might say: since their order is not indispensable, the sprinklings are not indispensable either. That is why ״לפר״ teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק finishes his answer. Since ״חקה״ does not cover the outside services, we need ״לפר״ to teach that those sprinklings are required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the outside services, the order is not indispensable. From that we might wrongly have concluded that the sprinklings themselves can be skipped. ״לפר״ stops that mistake and shows that the sprinklings are required, even though their order is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside, in the היכל, outside the קודש הקדשים
What he did counts
Their order
Sprinklings of blood

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, ״חקה״ makes only the inside יום הכפורים services indispensable, even in their order. For the outside services the order does not matter, but ״לפר״ teaches that the sprinklings themselves are still required.
steps.confusionAlert: Order and the act itself are two different things. The outside services can be done out of order, but the sprinklings cannot be skipped.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דְּבָרִים הַנַּעֲשִׂים בְּבִגְדֵי לָבָן בַּחוּץ,
phrases.english: but with things done in white garments outside,
phrases.notes: "Outside" here means in the היכל, still in white garments, but not in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: if he did one action before another,
what he did counts;
one might say: since their order is not indispensable,
the sprinklings are also not indispensable;
so it teaches us that they are.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל דְּבָרִים הַנַּעֲשִׂים בְּבִגְדֵי לָבָן בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer from step 20 by explaining what ״לפר״ adds for the outside services.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a mistaken conclusion (הוה אמינא) that the phrase is needed to block
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the order of the outside services is not indispensable, the sprinklings themselves are not indispensable either.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לפר״ teaches that the sprinklings are indispensable even though their order is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two kinds of requirement: whether an act must be done in order, and whether the act must be done at all.

steps.title: רב פפא challenges with a ברייתא about finishing the atonement
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks how we can say that רבי יהודה needs ״לפר״ to make the sprinklings indispensable. He quotes a ברייתא in which רבי עקיבא explains the פסוק ״וכלה מכפר את הקדש״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: Can you really say this? A ברייתא teaches: "And when he has finished atoning for the Sanctuary." If he did the atonement, he has finished; if he did not do the atonement, he has not finished. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the answer from Step 20. He starts quoting a ברייתא that will show רבי יהודה already has another source for this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק to mean that once the inside sprinklings are done, the service is finished, even before the leftover blood is poured out. This part of the ברייתא only sets the stage. The real challenge comes from רבי יהודה's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (strongly challenges a statement)
"And when he has finished atoning for the Sanctuary" (ויקרא 16:20)
He atoned, meaning he did the sprinklings that bring atonement
He finished the service

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to this:
And can you really say this?!
phrases.notes: He means: can you say that רבי יהודה learns from ״לפר״ that the sprinklings are indispensable?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
"And when he has finished atoning for the Sanctuary" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:20

phrases.english: if he atoned, he has finished;
phrases.notes: "Atoned" means he did the inside sprinklings. Then he counts as finished even without pouring out the leftover blood.

phrases.english: and if he did not atone, he has not finished.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer that ״לפר״ is needed according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה needs ״לפר״ to teach that the יום הכפורים sprinklings are indispensable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה learns this law from ״וכלה מכפר״, so ״לפר״ would be extra.

steps.title: רבי יהודה reads the same פסוק as making the full service indispensable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה turns the פסוק around: only if he finished does he achieve atonement. This shows that he learns from this פסוק that the sprinklings are indispensable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Why should we not say: If he finished, he achieved atonement; and if he did not finish, he did not achieve atonement?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב פפא's proof. רבי יהודה reads ״וכלה מכפר״ to mean that the atonement depends on doing everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, no atonement happens unless the whole service is completed, and that includes the sprinklings. So he already has a פסוק teaching that the sprinklings are indispensable. Then ״לפר״ cannot be needed for that, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Why should we not say (a way of offering a different reading)

steps.whyThisMatters: Since this answer fails, the גמרא must find a new reason why the ברייתא needs ״לפר״.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
For what reason should we not say:
if he finished, he achieved atonement;
and if he did not finish, he did not achieve atonement?
phrases.notes: So רבי יהודה already has this פסוק for the sprinklings. Why would he need ״לפר״?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֹאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב פפא started quoting in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה does not need ״לפר״ to make the sprinklings indispensable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's reading of ״וכלה מכפר את הקדש״ in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב פפא: ״לפר״ carries over three laws
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a new answer. ״לפר״ applies three laws to the bull of יום הכפורים: ״את״, ״בדם״, and ״בטבילה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: It is needed only for ״את״, ״בדם״, and ״בטבילה״.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives his own reason why ״לפר״ is needed. It does not teach that the details are indispensable. It brings over other laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three laws learned from the פסוק about the anointed כהן's bull (ויקרא 4:6): ״את״, ״בדם״, and ״בטבילה״. ״לפר״ teaches that these laws also apply to the bull of יום הכפורים. This way ״לפר״ is not extra, for either רבי עקיבא or רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for
"In the blood": the כהן dips his finger in the blood itself
Dipping the finger into the blood

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
It is needed only
for "et," "with blood," and "with immersion."
phrases.notes: These are short labels for three laws from ויקרא 4:6. Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording uses the word in square brackets instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְאֶת בְּדָם וּבִטְבִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was knocked down in Steps 22-23 with a new reason why ״לפר״ is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives ״לפר״ a new job: carrying over laws from another bull.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לפר״ teaches that the sprinklings of the יום הכפורים bull are indispensable.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״לפר״ applies the laws of ״את״, ״בדם״, and ״בטבילה״ to the bull of יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Beginning to explain ״את״
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to explain the first of the three laws, ״את״, quoting רב אחא בר יעקב. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for ״את״: רב אחא בר יעקב says: It is needed only to make fit...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up an explanation of the word ״את״. It starts quoting רב אחא בר יעקב, and his statement goes on into the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of רב פפא's three labels stands for a specific law. Here the גמרא begins to explain the first one, saying that ״את״ comes to make something fit. Exactly what it makes fit comes in the next words.

keyTerms.meaning: A small word in the פסוק (״את אצבעו״) that the גמרא reads as adding a law
To make fit or valid

phrases.english: "Et" —
phrases.notes: This is the ״את״ in ״את אצבעו״, "his finger," in ויקרא 4:6.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov says:
It is needed only to make fit
phrases.notes: His sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֶת״ – אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לֹא נִצְרְכָא לְהַכְשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first of the three laws that רב פפא listed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a label used in רב פפא's answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״את״ comes to make something fit; the details follow on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא בר יעקב: the word ״את״ comes to make something fit (the rest of his statement follows on the next amud).
